notes: Adaptive semantic LLM mode enabled via TKNT_SEMANTIC_ADAPTIVE_LLM; deterministic stage fallbacks are disabled.
Kept canonical cluster ids and tightened the program for a compact modern functional living room.
No new cluster was added because the brief is fully covered by seating, media, and optional storage support.
Tier hints are set to preserve the core seating and media pieces while allowing optional support to drop cleanly under density pressure.
Compact 14.28 m2 living room with high center-openness bias supports the core seating and media clusters strongly.
Support storage is useful but should remain optional and drop earlier than core anchors; prefer only one compact support item if surplus exists.
Pet/entry support is weakly supported by the brief; keep only if downstream logic detects explicit pet or entry need, and avoid over-pruning small items when surplus is comfortable.
Kept media and seating as primary due to brief focus and focal-surface support.
Preserved entry clearance and center openness as hard avoid regions for main seating and media.
Storage is secondary; entry/pet support is optional and lowest priority.

SemanticLayoutPlanner used the room profile registry as the canonical rule source.

Style policy compiled before layout planning; downstream geometry treats it as bias, not a hard override.
Request contract attached before tier count so explicit functional objects are protected from silent pruning.
Cluster main_seating: relaxed wall attachment for core social cluster to allow floating exploration.
Tier Count used deterministic utility, capacity, and bundle-preserving rules, plus Forge semantic tier-count hints when available.
Tier Count itself did not run an additional LLM call.
